messages:
support_jane: FYI - Customer AcmeMaps reports lots of 429s + timeouts on their Dedicated pool. They say autoscaling did not add replicas for ~6m during a traffic spike. Requesting help and repro steps.

custsuccess_amy: Escalation opened by AM. Customer says baseline min_replicas=2, surge to ~120 RPS caused queueing and 504s. They attached a sample curl and a short log.

support_jane: Minimal details from customer: model=gpt-large-8k, avg_tokens=120, concurrency=20 clients hitting at once, region=us-west-2, pool=dedi-usw2-acmemaps. They saw 429 throttle responses from our fronting layer while VMs were being provisioned.

eng_runtime_lead: @support_jane can you paste the exact curl they used and any error bodies? Also did they have "burst_capacity" enabled on their Dedicated contract?

support_jane: Here is the sample they sent: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/acme/predict \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large-8k","input":"summarize: ...","max_tokens":150}' \ 
  --parallel 20 --repeat 15
```

And a truncated error blob: 

```json
{"status":429,"message":"Capacity throttled: no healthy runner available","request_id":"req_0a1b2c"}
```

sre_matt: :eyes: That looks like requests hit the routing layer before the pool reached new replicas. We should check autoscaler event timeline and pool capacity. Did infra_lee's quota check run?

autoscale-bot: [event] 1812345690 autoscaler: scaleup initiated target=4 current=2; provisioning start; estimated ready in 90s
autoscale-bot: [event] 1812345750 autoscaler: scaleup complete current=4

eng_runtime_lead: autoscale timeline shows provisioning took ~60-70s, but customer saw throttles for ~6m. Two hypotheses: (1) the pool hit a queue/backpressure limiter before scale request reached scheduler due to rate of new connections, (2) node warmup/runner init was slower than VM provisioning and our routing kept returning 429 until runners registered.

infra_lee: I just checked underlying infra: no quota blocks, pool has capacity, but NVMe attach times spiked for that AZ at 1812345660 (I/O operations higher due to another tenant). Possible noisy-neighbor causing runner init delays.

support_jane: Customer also included a runner log snippet showing repeated TLS handshake timeouts during startup: 

```
[2026-03-15T12:01:05Z] runner-init: pulling model shards...
[2026-03-15T12:01:37Z] runner-init: TLS handshake failed, retrying (5/5)
[2026-03-15T12:02:08Z] runner-init: successful registration
```

eng_runtime_lead: That aligns. If runner registration delayed by tens of seconds per node, aggregate time to reach healthy capacity increases. We should: 1) reproduce in staging with same concurrency + model, 2) run profiling of runner init and NVMe attach, 3) consider short-term mitigation: enable reserved burst_capacity or increase min_replicas for this customer.

sre_matt: Repro plan suggestion: use k6 script to open 20 concurrent persistent connections for 5 minutes against a staging pool with min_replicas=2 and no burst. Observe: request latencies, HPA/ autoscaler events, runner registration times. I can run the load test at 1812346000 if that works for you.

custsuccess_amy: Please keep me posted — customer requests ETA on fix. They want either faster scale or guaranteed burst capacity.

eng_runtime_lead: Short-term action: ask customer to enable burst_capacity (if allowed) or set min_replicas=4 while we investigate. Long-term: we need better detection of runner init slowness and fallback to warm standby or reuse pre-warmed images for this SKU.

support_jane: I asked customer to temporarily bump min_replicas to 4 and enabled a one-time burst (billing note confirmed). They agreed to a repro window tomorrow.

infra_lee: Filed infra ticket INF-7821 to investigate NVMe attach latency spike in usw2-A. Also tagging noisy-tenant id tenant-77 for I/O throttling analysis.

eng_runtime_lead: I'll run the staging repro with the k6 script and attach logs. Quick command to reproduce locally for team: 

```bash
k6 run --vus 20 --duration 5m test-script.js # script posts same payload in a loop
```

support_jane: Updated customer — they appreciate the workaround. Opening internal ticket RED-13456 and assigning to eng-runtime + SRE for postmortem. Will keep channel updated. :thumbsup:

sre_matt: I'll be on the repro run and collect autoscaler / runner metrics (hpa.events, runner.register.time, attach.latency). If we confirm noisy neighbor, we can throttle tenant-77 IO at hypervisor level to protect runner init.

support_jane: Thanks all. Next sync in 24h after repro run.
